s1.syndrome_frame: Acute abdominal pain with radiating pain to the left thigh, accompanied by nausea, vomiting, and a palpable mass in the left buttock area, suggesting an obstructive and potentially strangulated hernia
salient_findings: Severe crampy pains in hypogastrium radiating down the back of the left thigh
Painful, non-reducible, tender mass in the left buttock area
History of intermittent abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting
key_facts: 45-year-old woman presented with severe abdominal pain
Pain radiates to the back of the left thigh
Nausea and vomiting accompanying the pain
Palpable, painful mass in the left buttock area
Mass measures 10 cm × 8 cm × 8 cm
Abdomen is soft with epigastrium tenderness and rebounding pain
Absence of intestinal gurgling sounds
History of calculous cholecystitis and cesarean delivery
Patient appears dehydrated and poorly nourished
Knee-flexed position due to pain
Intestinal obstruction and gallstone seen on abdominal X-ray
Incarcerated bowel loops beneath left gluteal muscles on ultrasonography
CT examination shows seroperitoneum, pneumoperitoneum, and low intestinal obstruction

shortlist.label: Sciatic hernia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presents with a palpable, painful mass in the left buttock area and radiating pain to the back of the left thigh, consistent with a sciatic hernia

shortlist.label: Strangulated femoral hernia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms of severe abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting, along with the presence of a palpable mass, are consistent with a strangulated hernia

shortlist.label: Incercerated Spigelian hernia
shortlist.why_kept: The location of the mass in the left buttock area and the patient's symptoms of abdominal pain and nausea are consistent with an incarcerated Spigelian hernia

shortlist.label: Internal hernia
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's symptoms of intestinal obstruction and the presence of a palpable mass are consistent with an internal hernia

shortlist.label: Obstructed inguinal hernia
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's symptoms of abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting, along with the presence of a palpable mass, are consistent with an obstructed inguinal hernia

raw.rationale: The presence of a palpable, painful mass in the left buttock area, radiating pain down the back of the left thigh, and imaging studies showing herniation through the left sciatic foramen containing a small bowel loop are consistent with a sciatic hernia.

rejected.label: Strangulated femoral hernia
rejected.why: The location of the hernia is in the buttock area, not the groin, which is more typical of femoral hernias.

rejected.label: Incercerated Spigelian hernia
rejected.why: The location of the hernia is not consistent with a Spigelian hernia, which typically occurs through the spigelian fascia near the semilunar line.

rejected.label: Internal hernia
rejected.why: The presence of a palpable mass in the left buttock area suggests an external hernia, rather than an internal hernia.

rejected.label: Obstructed inguinal hernia
rejected.why: The location of the hernia is in the buttock area, not the groin, which is more typical of inguinal hernias.
